title: Exclusive-JPMorgan CEO Dimon leads new cross-industry effort to tackle AI risks
excerpt: JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon is urging corporate leaders to join a U.S.-focused industry group to address risks posed by AI, as corporate America rapidly a...
content_html:
Nupur Anand

Wed, August 5, 2026 at 3:03 AM PDT 3 min read

By Nupur Anand

NEW YORK, Aug 5 (Reuters) - JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon is urging corporate leaders to join a U.S.-focused industry group to address risks posed by AI, as corporate America rapidly adopts the developing technology, two sources familiar with the matter said.

Dimon has personally ‌reached out to CEOs of other large and major regional banks and IT companies to enlist them in the initiative, which he is expanding ‌from a group that JPMorgan helped found called the Alliance for Critical Infrastructure, the sources said.

The ACI and Dimon have also communicated with other prospective members in an effort to schedule calls in ​August to discuss collaboration, the sources said.

The outreach, which started in July, includes more than 40 companies spanning financial services, energy, water, utilities, telecommunications, airlines, railroads and other critical infrastructure industries that rely heavily on technology, the sources said. The ACI has not disclosed results of the effort so far.

Dimon's views on the economy, regulation and technology are closely followed. As head of the largest U.S. bank, he has been among a small group of CEOs publicly warning about the risks posed by advanced AI ‌systems.

AI RISKS AND SAFEGUARDS

The initiative aims to develop a shared ⁠understanding of how AI is being used, the risks it poses and the safeguards needed, and to work with the Trump administration on those issues, the sources said. Recent cyberattacks on water systems in Minnesota and other states have increased the need ⁠for more information sharing across industries, the sources said.

JPMorgan was a founding member of the ACI alongside Mastercard, Berkshire Hathaway Energy and others. The organization was created to coordinate cross-sector resilience planning, share information, and respond to critical infrastructure threats, including cyber, physical and geopolitical risk. The group has a team that is also involved in refocusing the ACI ​and ​building up the AI effort.

Dimon said in a statement that the ACI leadership had seen the ​need to prioritize AI "years ago and got critical infrastructure companies working ‌together."

"We are proud to support this important work," Dimon said.

When asked about the initiative during a CNBC interview on Wednesday, Dimon said ACI's executive chairman Tom Fanning had set up the group a long time ago.

"I am like a support cast member," Dimon said. "This group will help interface with that (the government) and both give advice and take advice from the government."

努普尔·阿南德

路透纽约 8 月 5 日 - 两位知情人士称，随着美国企业界迅速采用这项正在发展的技术，摩根大通首席执行官杰米·戴蒙 (Jamie Dimon) 敦促企业领导人加入一个专注于美国的行业组织，以应对人工智能带来的风险。

消息人士称，戴蒙亲自联系了其他大型和主要区域银行和 IT 公司的首席执行官，让他们参与该计划，他正在从摩根大通帮助建立的一个名为“关键基础设施联盟”的组织中扩大该计划。

消息人士称，ACI 和戴蒙还与其他潜在成员进行了沟通，以安排 8 月份的电话讨论合作事宜。

消息人士称，此次推广活动于 7 月开始，涉及金融服务、能源、水务、公用事业、电信、航空、铁路和其他严重依赖技术的关键基础设施行业的 40 多家公司。 到目前为止，ACI 尚未透露这项工作的结果。

戴蒙对经济、监管和技术的看法受到密切关注。 作为美国最大银行的负责人，他是一小群公开警告先进人工智能系统带来风险的首席执行官之一。

人工智能风险和保障措施

消息人士称，该倡议旨在就人工智能的使用方式、其带来的风险和所需的保障措施达成共识，并就这些问题与特朗普政府合作。 消息人士称，最近明尼苏达州和其他州供水系统遭受的网络攻击增加了跨行业更多信息共享的需求。

摩根大通与万事达卡、伯克希尔哈撒韦能源公司等都是 ACI 的创始成员。 该组织的成立是为了协调跨部门的弹性规划、共享信息并应对关键基础设施威胁，包括网络、物理和地缘政治风险。 该小组有一个团队也参与重新调整 ACI 的重点和建立人工智能工作。

戴蒙在一份声明中表示，ACI 领导层“多年前就意识到需要优先考虑人工智能，并让关键基础设施公司合作”。

“我们很自豪能够支持这项重要的工作，”戴蒙说。

周三，戴蒙在接受 CNBC 采访时被问及这一举措时表示，ACI 执行主席汤姆·范宁 (Tom Fanning) 很久以前就成立了该组织。

“我就像一个支持演员，”戴蒙说。 “这个小组将帮助与政府建立联系，并提供建议并接受政府的建议。”
